Feature

Gardens on the roof

Architects in the northern districts are covering flat roofs with soil, herbs and tiny orchards. Residents harvest tomatoes above the traffic and swap seedlings across the narrow alleys between their buildings.

The movement began as a hobby, yet it now shapes municipal planning rules and the way new apartment blocks are designed.

Ines Calloway fires every bowl twice and sells them only at the Saturday market, where regulars line up before sunrise.
